request: Compose a 90-second Raag Bhairav × heavy metal piece in Bhairav key of E (Sa = E), in teentaal at 128 BPM.  Form, in avartans: intro (2) → mukhada stated twice (2) → antara (3) → mukhada returns (2) → back-to-back taans that accelerate into the end: a two-avartan taan_short running straight into a one-avartan taan_long (2 + 1). No tihai: the piece ends on the taans themselves.  Build the mukhada and the riff from one recognisable Bhairav motif, and let the antara lift that same idea into the upper octave before descending back into the mukhada, so the piece sounds developed rather than assembled. End with a hard stop: the final taan drives straight into the last sam, where the lead lands on upper Sa while guitar, bass and drums strike low Sa underneath it.  I will play the rhythm guitar live, so keep it playable on a standard six-string in E standard: anchor on the open low E, one core riff with a few variations, mostly eighth notes with only short sixteenth-note bursts.
